title: Normality of a strictly semistable model with smooth generic fibre
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed, def-weil-field] and $V\subseteq K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, meaning that for every $b\in K^\times$ either $b$ or $b^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Assume the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C$ be a strictly semistable $T$-curve with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then every local ring of $C$ is an integrally closed domain; in particular $C$ is normal and reduced [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. A $T$-curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with no separatedness or properness assumption. A $T$-curve is strictly semistable if, locally on the curve and $T$, it has an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] to $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$ or $\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv-a))$, for an open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ and $a\in A$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof, end of first paragraph, pp. 27--28: normality of semistable curves with smooth generic fibre, restricted to the strict case; primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this valuation-curve result.

proof.text: Fix $c\in C$, and choose a Zariski open neighbourhood $U$ of $c$ admitting the etale chart in the statement over a nonempty open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$. This base open is principal: the primes of $V$ are a finite chain, so if the open is proper, choose $f$ in the least excluded prime but outside the greatest included prime; its open is exactly $D(f)$. For the whole base take $f=1$. Thus $A=V_f$, with fraction field $K$. The valuation-ring theorem gives that $V$ is a normal domain, and localization gives the same for $A$.

source.place: Tags 00IC and 00GY; the finite-chain principal-open observation is written out in this step

proof.text: Consider a nodal chart $h:U\to W=\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv-a))$. If $a=0$ and $h(c)$ lies in $N=V(u,v)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$, then the image $h(U)$ is open: etale means flat and locally of finite presentation, so apply the open-map theorem. Its intersection with $N$ is a nonempty open subset of the spectrum of the domain $A$, hence contains the generic point $n_\eta$ of $N$. Choose $z\in U$ above $n_\eta$. This is a point of $U_\eta$, mapping to the node $(u,v)$ of $W_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}(K[u,v]/(uv))$.

source.place: Etale Definition Tag 02GI and flat-locally-finitely-presented openness; the generic-node specialization argument expands the strict-chart normality input of Temkin Proposition 4.3.1

proof.text:
This point $z$ cannot exist. The generic chart is etale by etale base change, hence flat. On affine neighbourhoods, localization of a flat ring map gives a flat local map
$H=(K[u,v]/(uv))_{(u,v)}\to\mathcal O_{U_\eta,z}$.
A flat local map is faithfully flat, and the universally injective theorem with module $H$ makes this map injective. In $H$, $u$ and $v$ are nonzero with product zero: before localization their annihilators are respectively $(v)$ and $(u)$, both contained in $(u,v)$, so no element inverted in $H$ kills either one. On the other hand $U_\eta$ is an open subscheme of the smooth generic fibre; smoothness is local on the source, and the smooth/geometrically-regular criterion with field extension $K/K$ makes its local rings regular. A regular local ring is a domain. The injective map from $H$ contradicts this. Consequently, when $a=0$, $h(c)$ lies in $D(u)\cup D(v)$, where the chart is respectively $A[u,u^{-1}]$ or $A[v,v^{-1}]$.

source.place: Tags 00HT, 00HR, 05CK, 00NP; etale base change is Morphisms Tag 02GO and smoothness/regularity is Varieties Tag 038X. These are exactly the cited generic tools; no Noetherian condition is imposed on A.

proof.text: For $a\ne0$ put $B=A[u,v]/(uv-a)$ and $F=\operatorname{Frac}(A)=K$. Reducing each mixed monomial by $uv=a$ writes every class as $c_0+\sum_{n>0}c_nu^n+\sum_{m>0}d_mv^m$, with finitely many coefficients in $A$. Under $u\mapsto u$, $v\mapsto a/u$ in $F[u,u^{-1}]$, the summands have distinct Laurent exponents; the negative coefficients are $d_ma^m$, so they vanish only if $d_m=0$. This proves injectivity and uniqueness of that normal form. Thus $B$ is a domain, and in $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=F(u)$ its localizations at $u$ and $v$ are $A[u,u^{-1}]$ and $A[v,v^{-1}]$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof, pp. 27--28, strict semistable chart input; explicit monomial reduction supplied by the agent (archival copy WANTED)

proof.text: The polynomial-normality and localization theorems make $B_u=A[u,u^{-1}]$ and $B_v=A[v,v^{-1}]$ normal domains. Inside $F(u)$ their intersection is $B$: write an element of $B_u$ as $\sum_n c_nu^n$, $c_n\in A$. Membership in $B_v$ says that the coefficients after substituting $u=a/v$, namely $c_na^n$, belong to $A$. In particular, for $n=-m<0$, $c_{-m}/a^m\in A$, so the negative term is $(c_{-m}/a^m)v^m$; the nonnegative terms are already in $A[u]$. Hence the element belongs to the normal form of step 4. Conversely $B$ lies in both localizations. An element of $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ integral over $B$ is integral over both localizations, therefore belongs to both by their normality, and so belongs to their intersection $B$. Thus $B$ is integrally closed; localization makes every $B_{\mathfrak p}$ an integrally closed domain. This is a normal ring by the definition.

source.place: Tags 030A and 00GY; the Laurent coefficient comparison and monic-polynomial argument are written out, rather than cited as a new chart theorem

proof.text: The polynomial chart $A[t]$ is a normal domain by polynomial normality, and is a normal ring because all its prime localizations are normal domains. The Laurent charts obtained in step 3 are normal for the same reason, using localization. The nonzero-parameter nodal chart is normal by steps 4--5. In all cases, after restricting $U$ to the inverse image of the indicated chart open containing $h(c)$ and then to an affine open neighbourhood of $c$, its coordinate ring is etale over the corresponding normal chart ring. Etale ascent of normality makes this coordinate ring normal. By the definition of a normal ring its localization at $c$, which is $\mathcal O_{C,c}$ because $U$ is Zariski open in $C$, is an integrally closed domain.

source.place: Tags 030A, 00GY and 033C (normality goes up along smooth maps, hence along etale maps); the latter is valid without Noetherian hypotheses, unlike Tag 025P

proof.text: Since $c$ was arbitrary, every local ring of $C$ is an integrally closed domain, giving normality. If an element of such a local ring is nilpotent, repeated use of the absence of zero divisors makes it zero. Thus every local ring is reduced, which is exactly the definition of a reduced scheme.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q88-9e97b1718 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. Its statement is byte-identical to the live new-targets copy. The source checks out: Temkin arXiv:0707.3953v3, §4.3 p.27 defines strictly semi-stable, and the end of the first paragraph of the proof of Prop 4.3.1 (pp.27-28) uses exactly this normality. I read every cited node's statement: 00IC, 00GY, 030A, 02GO, 00HT, 00HR, 05CK (N=H), 01V6, 038X (L=K), 00NP, and 033C, which needs no Noetherian hypothesis, as a possibly non-Noetherian V requires. Each step checks. Step 1: a nonempty open of a finite chain is D(f) with f in p_{k+1} minus p_k, so A=V_f is a normal domain. Steps 2-3: if a=0 and h(c) lies on the node line, openness of h(U) gives a point z over the generic node. A faithfully flat, hence injective, map from (K[u,v]/(uv))_{(u,v)}, where Ann(u)=(v) and Ann(v)=(u) so u,v stay nonzero, cannot land in a regular local domain of the smooth generic fibre. So when a=0, h(c) lies in a Laurent chart. Steps 4-5: for a nonzero, the normal-form embedding into F[u,u^-1] works, and B_u ∩ B_v = B because a^m divides c_{-m]. I re-derived both, so B is normal. Step 6: the ascent uses a Zariski-open affine and 033C. Step 7: reducedness follows from the definition. Edge cases checked: C empty, V=K, a a unit, a=0 away from the node, disconnected etale charts. There are no new nodes. No DAG or blueprint duplicate turned up from rg on semistable, uv-a, Laurent and normal. There is no cycle, and the only citer is cofinality. No SGA is used. I accept the generic tool_uses from other units (sk-thm-p1, sk-thm-properbasechange, sk-prop-sf-cbc, sk-thm-picard-duality). Minor and not faults: blueprint.from.place was shortened but still names the exact Temkin sentence, and the report mentions a citations.json that is not in the commit. No fixes.
